terms.title: Account ID
terms.summary: A typed Norito pointer uniquely referencing a Nexus account, including network, data-space UUID, domain, name, and checksum fields.
terms.definition: A typed Norito pointer uniquely referencing a Nexus account, including network, data-space UUID, domain, name, and checksum fields.
terms.tagline: Enables human-readable addresses while preventing typos and cross-chain confusion.

terms.title: Account Lifecycle
terms.summary: The governed process that creates, updates, and retires Nexus accounts, ensuring every change is validated by the Iroha Virtual Machine and the hosting data space's policy.
terms.definition: The governed process that creates, updates, and retires Nexus accounts, ensuring every change is validated by the Iroha Virtual Machine and the hosting data space's policy.
terms.tagline: Creates.

terms.title: Action
terms.summary: The executable portion of a trigger or automation, defining which Iroha Special Instructions or Kotodama call runs when conditions are met.
terms.definition: The executable portion of a trigger or automation, defining which Iroha Special Instructions or Kotodama call runs when conditions are met.
terms.tagline: Separates logic from scheduling, making smart contracts easier to audit and compose.

terms.title: Activation Slot
terms.summary: The ledger slot pre-scheduled in a governed manifest where an approved runtime upgrade or configuration change becomes active across all lanes.
terms.definition: The ledger slot pre-scheduled in a governed manifest where an approved runtime upgrade or configuration change becomes active across all lanes.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Admission
terms.summary: The transaction intake stage where gateways and validators enforce roles, quotas, fees, and Start-Time Fair Queuing so only policy-compliant work enters execution.
terms.definition: The transaction intake stage where gateways and validators enforce roles, quotas, fees, and Start-Time Fair Queuing so only policy-compliant work enters execution.
terms.tagline: Provides seamless access to SORA Nexus services.

terms.title: Adoption
terms.summary: Adoption describes the rate at which people, partners, and institutions begin using SORA products, liquidity, and governance tooling in real-world contexts.
terms.definition: Adoption describes the rate at which people, partners, and institutions begin using SORA products, liquidity, and governance tooling in real-world contexts.

terms.title: Aggregation
terms.summary: The bundling phase collecting each data space's state roots, proofs, and data-availability artifacts into lane blocks prior to consensus.
terms.definition: The bundling phase collecting each data space's state roots, proofs, and data-availability artifacts into lane blocks prior to consensus.
terms.tagline: Combines parallel lane outputs into a single verifiable state transition.

terms.title: Agile Coretime
terms.summary: A flexible market where Polkadot sells coretime slices directly through brokered deals instead of fixed auctions.
terms.definition: Agile coretime lets projects purchase future execution capacity programmatically, smoothing demand and reducing the need for large upfront bids. It complements auctions and crowdloans by offering shorter-term or incremental commitments.

terms.title: Algorithmic Stability
terms.summary: Mechanisms that maintain stable asset value through programmatic supply adjustments—core to TBCD and SORA's monetary policy.
terms.definition: Algorithmic stability uses smart contracts and liquidity incentives to keep stablecoins near target value. SORA's Token Bonding Curve Dollar (TBCD) and Kensetsu architecture rely on algorithmic stability backed by governance oversight.

terms.title: AMM
terms.summary: Automated Market Maker - a protocol that uses mathematical formulas to price assets and provide liquidity automatically. Polkaswap uses AMM technology combined with liquidity ag…
terms.definition: Automated Market Maker - a protocol that uses mathematical formulas to price assets and provide liquidity automatically. Polkaswap uses AMM technology combined with liquidity aggregation to provide efficient trading with reduced impermanent loss.

terms.title: Analytics
terms.summary: Analytics covers the dashboards, telemetry, and research teams tracking SORA network health, liquidity depth, bridge flow, and ecosystem growth.
terms.definition: Analytics covers the dashboards, telemetry, and research teams tracking SORA network health, liquidity depth, bridge flow, and ecosystem growth.

terms.title: Apollo Protocol
terms.summary: A SORA ecosystem initiative focused on community-built tooling, analytics, and governance support for Polkaswap and SORA v3 upgrades.
terms.definition: Apollo Protocol coordinates community contributors who research tokenomics, publish knowledge base updates, and build automation for SORA releases. The group produces roadmap briefings, glossary enhancements, and documentation that keep builders aligned with Kensetsu, TBCD, and Polkaswap milestones.

terms.title: APOLLO Token
terms.summary: A community reward token used by the Apollo Protocol to incentivize research, documentation, and tooling for the SORA ecosystem.
terms.definition: The APOLLO token compensates contributors who publish technical research, produce analytics, and maintain documentation that supports SORA builders. Distribution is coordinated by the Apollo Protocol collective based on measurable ecosystem contributions.

terms.title: Assembly
terms.summary: One of SORA Parliament's two chambers, representing the wider stakeholder base with stake-weighted or one-person-one-vote selection and on-chain proposal rights.
terms.definition: One of SORA Parliament's two chambers, representing the wider stakeholder base with stake-weighted or one-person-one-vote selection and on-chain proposal rights.
terms.tagline: Gives token holders direct influence over network upgrades and policy changes.

terms.title: Asset Definition ID
terms.summary: A typed handle that points to an asset schema within a data space, allowing contracts to reference assets without ambiguous string parsing.
terms.definition: A typed handle that points to an asset schema within a data space, allowing contracts to reference assets without ambiguous string parsing.
terms.tagline: Points to an asset schema within a data space.

terms.title: Asset Tokenization
terms.summary: The process of issuing blockchain-based tokens that represent ownership of real-world or digital assets. SORA leverages tokenization to bring commodities, currencies, and projects on-chain.
terms.definition: Asset tokenization converts claims on physical or financial assets into programmable tokens. In SORA, tokenization is used to represent real-world assets, raise capital for new ventures, and create liquidity by listing these tokens on Polkaswap or other DeFi applications.

terms.title: Asynchronous Backing
terms.summary: A Polkadot upgrade that lets parachains submit work in parallel stages to raise throughput and lower latency.
terms.definition: Asynchronous backing separates block production, validation, and availability into overlapping phases. Validators can approve availability for one block while producing the next, increasing parachain capacity without compromising security.

terms.title: Attestations
terms.summary: Signed statements - typically using ML-DSA-87 - that certify new data spaces, DA proofs, or governance actions before the network accepts them.
terms.definition: Signed statements - typically using ML-DSA-87 - that certify new data spaces, DA proofs, or governance actions before the network accepts them.
terms.tagline: Empowers the community to shape the network's evolution.

terms.title: Attesters
terms.summary: Specialized actors who verify erasure-coded shards and proofs, then issue DA certificates so validators can rely on the data without downloading everything.
terms.definition: Specialized actors who verify erasure-coded shards and proofs, then issue DA certificates so validators can rely on the data without downloading everything.
terms.tagline: Guarantees that transaction data remains accessible and verifiable.

terms.title: Parachain Auctions
terms.summary: Candle-style events where Polkadot and Kusama projects bond DOT or KSM to lease parachain slots.
terms.definition: Parachain slot auctions determine which projects gain access to shared security for a fixed lease period. Bids accumulate until a randomized ending block is selected, encouraging honest bidding and staking participation through crowdloans.

terms.title: Automation
terms.summary: Deterministic, on-ledger workflows composed of conditions, actions, and budgets that let operators schedule recurring payments or policy checks without off-chain bots.
terms.definition: Deterministic, on-ledger workflows composed of conditions, actions, and budgets that let operators schedule recurring payments or policy checks without off-chain bots.
terms.tagline: Ensures fair resource allocation across the network.

terms.title: Bakong
terms.summary: Cambodia's national digital payment system built on blockchain technology by SORAMITSU. Bakong is one of the most successful CBDC implementations, with over 20 million users and…
terms.definition: Cambodia's national digital payment system built on blockchain technology by SORAMITSU. Bakong is one of the most successful CBDC implementations, with over 20 million users and $70 billion in transactions, demonstrating the potential of blockchain-based digital currencies.

terms.title: Bear Market
terms.summary: A market environment characterized by falling prices and defensive positioning.
terms.definition: Bear markets reflect sustained declines—commonly defined as drops of 20% or more—driven by risk aversion, deleveraging, or macro shocks. Strategies include conserving liquidity, diversifying collateral, and accelerating development to prepare for the next cycle.

terms.title: Bech32 Format
terms.summary: The human-readable string encoding used for Nexus account addresses, derived from the canonical binary layout and protected with a Blake2b checksum.
terms.definition: The human-readable string encoding used for Nexus account addresses, derived from the canonical binary layout and protected with a Blake2b checksum.
terms.tagline: Enables Nexus account addresses.

terms.title: BFT Consensus
terms.summary: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus is a consensus mechanism that allows a distributed system to reach agreement even when some nodes fail or act maliciously. SORA v3 uses…
terms.definition: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus is a consensus mechanism that allows a distributed system to reach agreement even when some nodes fail or act maliciously. SORA v3 uses BFT consensus derived from Hyperledger Iroha 3's architecture, providing high-throughput transaction processing with deterministic finality. This differs from SORA v2's Substrate-based consensus, offering improved security and performance for enterprise-grade applications including CBDCs.

terms.title: Bitcoin (BTC)
terms.summary: The first decentralized cryptocurrency, created by Satoshi Nakamoto in 2009 with a capped 21 million supply.
terms.definition: Bitcoin combines proof-of-work consensus, public-key cryptography, and halving-based issuance to secure peer-to-peer digital cash. Its monetary policy and liquidity cycles influence broader crypto markets, including assets listed on Polkaswap.

terms.title: BLAKE2b
terms.summary: The fast hash function used for tasks like leader selection, account checksums, and pseudo-randomness inside the SUMERAGI pipeline.
terms.definition: The fast hash function used for tasks like leader selection, account checksums, and pseudo-randomness inside the SUMERAGI pipeline.
terms.tagline: Ensures data integrity and enables secure verification across the network.

terms.title: Blinded CIDs
terms.summary: Obfuscated content identifiers within SoraNet that preserve privacy by hiding the underlying data reference while still allowing routing and settlement.
terms.definition: Obfuscated content identifiers within SoraNet that preserve privacy by hiding the underlying data reference while still allowing routing and settlement.
terms.tagline: Preserve privacy by hiding the underlying data reference while still allowing routing and settlement.

terms.title: Blockchain
terms.summary: A distributed ledger technology that maintains a continuously growing list of records secured using cryptography. SORA operates on blockchain technology, currently using Substra…
terms.definition: A distributed ledger technology that maintains a continuously growing list of records secured using cryptography. SORA operates on blockchain technology, currently using Substrate framework and transitioning to Hyperledger Iroha for enhanced enterprise capabilities.

terms.title: Blockchain Architecture
terms.summary: The design of blockchain components, including consensus, networking, data storage, and execution layers.
terms.definition: Blockchain architecture defines how nodes reach consensus, manage state, and upgrade over time. Reference models such as Substrate or Hyperledger Iroha separate the runtime, networking, and application layers to support modular upgrades and interoperability.

terms.title: Blockchain Culture
terms.summary: The shared narratives, rituals, and community norms that influence how blockchain networks grow and govern themselves.
terms.definition: Blockchain culture covers memes, language, social coordination, and incentive structures that shape contributor behavior. Understanding culture helps projects design governance, communication, and incentive programs that resonate with their communities.

links.label: Harvard Business Review – What Blockchain Can Do

terms.title: Blockchain Development
terms.summary: Engineering decentralized applications, smart contracts, and infrastructure that run on blockchain networks.
terms.definition: Blockchain development spans consensus clients, runtime modules, front-end interfaces, and integrations. Tooling such as Substrate, Hyperledger Iroha, and smart-contract frameworks enable teams to build features like Polkaswap, Kensetsu vaults, and cross-chain bridges.

terms.title: Blockchain Economics
terms.summary: The study of how token supply, incentives, and governance interact to sustain decentralized networks.
terms.definition: Blockchain economics analyzes monetary policy, reward distribution, and treasury design to keep participants aligned. Frameworks like the SORA token bonding curve illustrate how supply elasticity and governance controlled reserves stabilize ecosystem growth.

terms.title: Bokolo Cash
terms.summary: The Central Bank of Solomon Islands' digital currency pilot developed by SORAMITSU. Bokolo Cash demonstrates how SORA technology powers retail CBDCs with mobile-first payments.
terms.definition: Bokolo Cash is a CBDC project launched by the Central Bank of Solomon Islands and SORAMITSU. It uses SORA technology to deliver secure wallets, point-of-sale integrations, and compliance workflows that make digital currency available to citizens and merchants without traditional banking infrastructure.

terms.title: Bonding Curve
terms.summary: A smart contract that manages the supply of XOR in a rational way without human involvement. The TBC automatically adjusts XOR supply based on economic conditions to maintain price stability, expanding supply during growth and contracting during decline.
terms.definition: A smart contract that manages the supply of XOR in a rational way without human involvement. The TBC automatically adjusts XOR supply based on economic conditions to maintain price stability, expanding supply during growth and contracting during decline.

terms.title: Bonk (BONK)
terms.summary: A Solana-based meme token launched in 2022 that distributed a large airdrop to builders and NFT projects to revive Solana activity.
terms.definition: BONK runs on the Solana blockchain and uses token airdrops, liquidity incentives, and NFT partnerships to encourage ecosystem engagement. It highlights how meme assets can accelerate network usage outside of SORA.

terms.title: Borderless Finance
terms.summary: Borderless finance refers to financial services accessible globally without geographic restrictions. SORA enables borderless DeFi through permissionless access to Polkaswap, staking, and governance.
terms.definition: Borderless finance refers to financial services accessible globally without geographic restrictions. SORA enables borderless DeFi through permissionless access to Polkaswap, staking, and governance.

terms.title: Borrowing
terms.summary: Taking on debt against posted collateral using smart contracts that enforce repayment and liquidation rules.
terms.definition: Borrowing in DeFi involves locking approved collateral to mint or draw assets, paying stability fees until the position is closed. Kensetsu vaults on SORA apply governance-defined collateral ratios and liquidation procedures to keep the system solvent while providing access to KUSD or other approved assets.

terms.title: Bridges
terms.summary: Bridges are interoperability protocols that move assets and data between SORA and external chains so liquidity can circulate without centralized custodians.
terms.definition: Bridges are interoperability protocols that move assets and data between SORA and external chains so liquidity can circulate without centralized custodians.

terms.title: Budget
terms.summary: The TEU and fee allowance assigned to a trigger or automation, preventing unlimited compute or bandwidth consumption.
terms.definition: The TEU and fee allowance assigned to a trigger or automation, preventing unlimited compute or bandwidth consumption.
terms.tagline: Caps resource usage per operation so no single transaction can monopolize the network.

terms.title: Bull Market
terms.summary: A prolonged period of rising asset prices accompanied by expanding liquidity and optimism.
terms.definition: Bull markets occur when demand consistently outpaces supply, often supported by macro trends, innovation, or positive narratives. Participants may increase risk exposure, but prudent treasury management still prepares for eventual reversals.

terms.title: Buyback-and-burn
terms.summary: A tokenomic mechanism where tokens are purchased from the market and permanently destroyed. PSWAP uses a buyback-and-burn model where 0.3% of trading fees are used to buy PSWAP …
terms.definition: A tokenomic mechanism where tokens are purchased from the market and permanently destroyed. PSWAP uses a buyback-and-burn model where 0.3% of trading fees are used to buy PSWAP tokens from the market and burn them, reducing total supply and potentially increasing token value.

terms.title: Byzantine Fault Tolerance
terms.summary: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) is a consensus property ensuring network operation even when some nodes act maliciously. SORA uses BFT-based SUMERAGI consensus for deterministic finality.
terms.definition: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) is a consensus property ensuring network operation even when some nodes act maliciously. SORA uses BFT-based SUMERAGI consensus for deterministic finality.

terms.title: Canonical Primitives
terms.summary: The curated list of cryptographic algorithms (Poseidon2, DEEP-FRI, ML-DSA-87, etc.) that SORA Nexus mandates to keep security assumptions consistent across data spaces.
terms.definition: The curated list of cryptographic algorithms (Poseidon2, DEEP-FRI, ML-DSA-87, etc.) that SORA Nexus mandates to keep security assumptions consistent across data spaces.
terms.tagline: SORA Nexus mandates to keep security assumptions consistent across data spaces.

terms.title: CBDC
terms.summary: Central Bank Digital Currency - a digital form of a country's fiat currency issued by the central bank. SORAMITSU has successfully deployed multiple CBDCs including Cambodia's B…
terms.definition: Central Bank Digital Currency - a digital form of a country's fiat currency issued by the central bank. SORAMITSU has successfully deployed multiple CBDCs including Cambodia's Bakong (8.5M users, $15.5M in payments), Lao CBDC pilot, and Fiji CBDC exploration. These blockchain-based systems enable financial inclusion, cross-border remittances, and interoperable digital payments.

terms.title: Ceres
terms.summary: A SORA-based DeFi suite providing launchpad services, stablecoins, and liquidity tools that complement Polkaswap.
terms.definition: Ceres offers decentralized applications such as Demeter Farming, SORA Card integrations, and liquidity vaults built on the SORA network. Its tooling accelerates adoption of Polkaswap pairs and supports Kensetsu stablecoin use cases.
terms.tagline: Provides essential DeFi infrastructure for projects building on SORA.

terms.title: Chainlink
terms.summary: A decentralized oracle network that provides tamper-resistant data feeds and automation services to smart contracts. SORA integrates Chainlink oracles to bridge real-world data for DeFi and RWA products.
terms.definition: Chainlink delivers cryptographic proofs and reliable data to smart contracts. On SORA, Chainlink price feeds and automation support Polkaswap trading pairs, collateral monitoring for tokenized assets, and cross-chain messaging for enterprise integrations.

terms.title: Circuit Breakers
terms.summary: Automated controls that throttle lane admission, message sizes, or DA limits when the system detects stress, preventing resource exhaustion.
terms.definition: Automated controls that throttle lane admission, message sizes, or DA limits when the system detects stress, preventing resource exhaustion.
terms.tagline: Ensures privacy by routing traffic through multiple relay nodes.

terms.title: Circuit-Breaker State
terms.summary: The telemetry surface exposing which circuit breakers are engaged, letting operators observe throttling events and recovery in real time.
terms.definition: The telemetry surface exposing which circuit breakers are engaged, letting operators observe throttling events and recovery in real time.
terms.tagline: Ensures privacy by routing traffic through multiple relay nodes.

terms.title: Citizenship
terms.summary: A status in the SORA Parliament governance system where individuals become citizens by posting XOR bonds. Citizens are randomly selected through sortition to participate in vari…
terms.definition: A status in the SORA Parliament governance system where individuals become citizens by posting XOR bonds. Citizens are randomly selected through sortition to participate in various governance bodies and make decisions about XOR allocation to productive projects.

terms.title: Collateral
terms.summary: Assets pledged to secure loans or stablecoin issuance. Collateral design determines the safety of SORA's future lending products.
terms.definition: Collateral provides assurance that loans can be repaid or liquidated. SORA plans to accept XOR, stablecoins, and real-world assets as collateral for Kensetsu vaults, combining decentralized governance with transparent risk metrics.

links.label: SORA Token Bonding Curve Dollar Explained

terms.title: Collateralized Locks
terms.summary: Escrowed funds backing offline-offline vouchers, providing settlement guarantees until reconciliation clears or revokes the transfer.
terms.definition: Escrowed funds backing offline-offline vouchers, providing settlement guarantees until reconciliation clears or revokes the transfer.
terms.tagline: Enables secure offline payments that settle atomically when parties reconnect.

terms.title: Commitments
terms.summary: Cryptographic bindings (Merkle roots, Poseidon2 hashes) tying execution traces, memory, or DA shards to a block for auditing without re-running computation.
terms.definition: Cryptographic bindings (Merkle roots, Poseidon2 hashes) tying execution traces, memory, or DA shards to a block for auditing without re-running computation.
terms.tagline: Lets anyone verify state correctness by checking a small proof instead of replaying all transactions.

terms.title: Commit Window
terms.summary: The bounded number of slots (Delta <= 2) within which SUMERAGI must finalize a proposal, ensuring predictable finality even under adversarial network conditions.
terms.definition: The bounded number of slots (Delta <= 2) within which SUMERAGI must finalize a proposal, ensuring predictable finality even under adversarial network conditions.
terms.tagline: Essential component of the SORA Nexus architecture.

terms.title: Community
terms.summary: The SORA community comprises developers, validators, liquidity providers, governance participants, and users who collectively shape the network direction through proposals, discussions, and on-chain voting.
terms.definition: The SORA community comprises developers, validators, liquidity providers, governance participants, and users who collectively shape the network direction through proposals, discussions, and on-chain voting.

terms.title: Compute Lane
terms.summary: A dedicated lane running governed compute manifests—like SoraNet streaming or heavy analytics—without interfering with core transaction lanes.
terms.definition: A dedicated lane running governed compute manifests—like SoraNet streaming or heavy analytics—without interfering with core transaction lanes.
terms.tagline: Isolates resource-intensive workloads so they don't slow down regular transactions.

terms.title: Compute Manifest
terms.summary: The on-chain specification describing which workloads a compute lane accepts, how they're routed, and which data spaces they can access.
terms.definition: The on-chain specification describing which workloads a compute lane accepts, how they're routed, and which data spaces they can access.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Concurrency
terms.summary: The ability of a system to handle multiple tasks or processes overlapping in time.
terms.definition: Concurrency techniques—such as threads, async executors, and message passing—allow software to utilize multi-core hardware and keep I/O operations non-blocking. SORA infrastructure written in Rust relies on disciplined concurrency to maintain reliability.

terms.title: Condition
terms.summary: The predicate part of a trigger (time-based, event-based, or receipt-based) that must evaluate true before its actions consume TEU budget.
terms.definition: The predicate part of a trigger (time-based, event-based, or receipt-based) that must evaluate true before its actions consume TEU budget.
terms.tagline: Ensures fair resource allocation across the network.

terms.title: Consensus
terms.summary: The mechanism by which blockchain networks agree on the validity of transactions and maintain a consistent state. SORA v2 uses Substrate-based consensus mechanisms (NPoS - Nomin…
terms.definition: The mechanism by which blockchain networks agree on the validity of transactions and maintain a consistent state. SORA v2 uses Substrate-based consensus mechanisms (NPoS - Nominated Proof of Stake). SORA v3 will use Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus derived from Hyperledger Iroha 3's architecture, providing high-throughput transaction processing with deterministic finality, making it suitable for enterprise applications and CBDCs.

terms.title: Coretime
terms.summary: The compute resource that Polkadot sells to projects so they can execute workloads on relay-chain validators.
terms.definition: Coretime packages validator execution capacity into timeslices that projects buy via auctions or agile markets. Managing coretime commitments helps parachains plan throughput needs, budget DOT expenditures, and coordinate upgrades.

terms.title: Council
terms.summary: A governance body in SORA's current Polkadot v1 governance system that consists of elected members who can propose referenda and veto dangerous proposals. The council plays a key role in the governance process before transitioning to the SORA Parliament.
terms.definition: A governance body in SORA's current Polkadot v1 governance system that consists of elected members who can propose referenda and veto dangerous proposals. The council plays a key role in the governance process before transitioning to the SORA Parliament.

terms.title: Council Motion
terms.summary: A proposal submitted by the SORA Council in the current governance system. When a council motion is approved, it triggers a Democracy Referendum where token holders can vote on …
terms.definition: A proposal submitted by the SORA Council in the current governance system. When a council motion is approved, it triggers a Democracy Referendum where token holders can vote on the proposal, enabling community participation in governance decisions.

terms.title: Cross-Border Corridors
terms.summary: A highlighted use case where Nexus hosts multi-jurisdiction payment networks with deterministic policy enforcement and shared liquidity.
terms.definition: A highlighted use case where Nexus hosts multi-jurisdiction payment networks with deterministic policy enforcement and shared liquidity.
terms.tagline: Essential component of the SORA Nexus architecture.

terms.title: Cross-border Payments
terms.summary: Financial transactions between parties in different countries. CBDC implementations like Bakong enable faster, cheaper, and more efficient cross-border remittances by using bloc…
terms.definition: Financial transactions between parties in different countries. CBDC implementations like Bakong enable faster, cheaper, and more efficient cross-border remittances by using blockchain technology to reduce intermediaries and settlement times.

terms.title: Cross-Chain
terms.summary: The ability to transfer assets and data between different blockchain networks. SORA enables cross-chain functionality through bridges and interoperability protocols, allowing us…
terms.definition: The ability to transfer assets and data between different blockchain networks. SORA enables cross-chain functionality through bridges and interoperability protocols, allowing users to trade assets from different blockchains on Polkaswap.

terms.title: Crowdloans
terms.summary: Campaigns that let token holders bond assets to support a project's parachain auction bid.
terms.definition: Crowdloans escrow contributor DOT or KSM on the relay chain, returning the stake after the lease while projects distribute rewards separately. They democratize access to parachain slots and align community incentives with network growth.

terms.title: Cryptography
terms.summary: Cryptography in blockchain provides security through digital signatures, hash functions, and encryption. SORA uses Ed25519, BLAKE2b, and other primitives to secure accounts and transactions.
terms.definition: Cryptography in blockchain provides security through digital signatures, hash functions, and encryption. SORA uses Ed25519, BLAKE2b, and other primitives to secure accounts and transactions.

terms.title: Crypto Market Cycles
terms.summary: Recurring bull and bear phases observed in cryptocurrency markets. Understanding cycles informs staking, liquidity, and treasury decisions in the SORA ecosystem.
terms.definition: Crypto market cycles describe periods of expansion and contraction driven by macro events, liquidity, and investor sentiment. SORA tracks these cycles to plan token issuance, liquidity incentives, and treasury diversification so that builders can deploy capital efficiently.

terms.title: Curve25519
terms.summary: The elliptic-curve key exchange primitive paired with Kyber768 in SoraNet's hybrid post-quantum handshake.
terms.definition: The elliptic-curve key exchange primitive paired with Kyber768 in SoraNet's hybrid post-quantum handshake.
terms.tagline: Foundation for secure key exchange and digital signatures.

terms.title: DA Certificates
terms.summary: Signed attestations from validators or attesters confirming that required data-availability samples were checked and can be reconstructed.
terms.definition: Signed attestations from validators or attesters confirming that required data-availability samples were checked and can be reconstructed.
terms.tagline: Guarantees that transaction data remains accessible and verifiable.

terms.title: DA Sampling
terms.summary: Fetching a limited number of erasure-coded shards per data space to statistically guarantee recoverability without downloading entire envelopes.
terms.definition: Fetching a limited number of erasure-coded shards per data space to statistically guarantee recoverability without downloading entire envelopes.
terms.tagline: Reduces bandwidth requirements for validators while maintaining strong availability guarantees.

terms.title: DA Sampling Budget
terms.summary: The governance cap (e.g., q_total <= 2048) on how many DA samples can be performed per slot so verification stays within hardware limits.
terms.definition: The governance cap (e.g., q_total <= 2048) on how many DA samples can be performed per slot so verification stays within hardware limits.
terms.tagline: Ensures fair resource allocation across the network.

terms.title: DA Sampling Confidence
terms.summary: The probability, computed via combinatorics, that malicious withholding will be detected given the chosen sample count and committee size.
terms.definition: The probability, computed via combinatorics, that malicious withholding will be detected given the chosen sample count and committee size.
terms.tagline: Guarantees that transaction data remains accessible and verifiable.

terms.title: Data Availability
terms.summary: The guarantee that every transaction's payload can be reconstructed by honest parties, even when the original submitter goes offline.
terms.definition: The guarantee that every transaction's payload can be reconstructed by honest parties, even when the original submitter goes offline.
terms.tagline: Prevents data withholding attacks that could halt chain progress or hide fraud.

terms.title: Data Availability Layer
terms.summary: The combined erasure-coding, sampling, proving, and attestation system enforcing data availability across public and private data spaces.
terms.definition: The combined erasure-coding, sampling, proving, and attestation system enforcing data availability across public and private data spaces.
terms.tagline: Lets light clients verify block data exists without downloading entire blocks.

terms.title: Data Envelope
terms.summary: The serialized bundle of transactions, proofs, and metadata that a data space contributes to a lane block before erasure coding.
terms.definition: The serialized bundle of transactions, proofs, and metadata that a data space contributes to a lane block before erasure coding.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Data Space Directory
terms.summary: The on-chain registry mapping DSIDs to owners, routing endpoints, and policy metadata so gateways know how to handle each space.
terms.definition: The on-chain registry mapping DSIDs to owners, routing endpoints, and policy metadata so gateways know how to handle each space.
terms.tagline: Provides seamless access to SORA Nexus services.

terms.title: Data Space ID
terms.summary: A typed pointer that identifies which data space an account, asset, or instruction belongs to, enabling cross-space safety checks.
terms.definition: A typed pointer that identifies which data space an account, asset, or instruction belongs to, enabling cross-space safety checks.
terms.tagline: Identifies which data space an account.

terms.title: Data Spaces
terms.summary: Sovereignty-preserving partitions allowing different jurisdictions or applications to share the same ledger without sharing private data.
terms.definition: Sovereignty-preserving partitions allowing different jurisdictions or applications to share the same ledger without sharing private data.
terms.tagline: Enables enterprises and regulators to participate in SORA while maintaining data isolation.

terms.title: Decentralization
terms.summary: Decentralization is the principle of distributing power across validators, councils, and citizens so no single entity can control the SORA economy.
terms.definition: Decentralization is the principle of distributing power across validators, councils, and citizens so no single entity can control the SORA economy.

terms.title: Decentralized Exchange
terms.summary: A decentralized exchange (DEX) enables peer-to-peer trading without intermediaries. Polkaswap is SORA DEX, offering multi-source liquidity, low fees, and permissionless token swaps.
terms.definition: A decentralized exchange (DEX) enables peer-to-peer trading without intermediaries. Polkaswap is SORA DEX, offering multi-source liquidity, low fees, and permissionless token swaps.

terms.title: Deep-fri
terms.summary: The low-degree testing protocol inside FASTPQ STARK proofs that lets verifiers check massive execution traces with logarithmic work.
terms.definition: The low-degree testing protocol inside FASTPQ STARK proofs that lets verifiers check massive execution traces with logarithmic work.

In SORA v3 tokenomics, KUSD is used to pay builders instead of XOR. To maintain the KUSD peg, 19.5% of all SORA network transaction fees are allocated for buyback and burning of KUSD. terms.title: Proof of Stake (PoS)
terms.summary: A consensus mechanism where validators stake tokens to secure the network. SORA v2 uses NPoS on Substrate while SORA v3 moves toward BFT consensus.
terms.definition: Proof of Stake selects validators based on staked assets rather than energy expenditure. The model incentivizes honest behavior by slashing or rewarding stake. SORA references PoS to explain historical network phases and to contrast with Hyperledger Iroha's BFT consensus.

terms.title: Proof of Work (PoW)
terms.summary: A consensus method where miners expend computational energy to propose blocks and earn rewards.
terms.definition: Proof of Work secures networks such as Bitcoin by requiring miners to solve cryptographic puzzles. The difficulty adjusts to maintain steady block production, making attacks costly because adversaries must control the majority of hashing power.

terms.title: Redenomination
terms.summary: The process of adjusting token denominations without changing total value. SORA redenominated XOR in 2020 to improve usability and align token supply with long-term monetary policy.
terms.definition: Redenomination changes the nominal unit of account by splitting or combining circulating supply while preserving proportional ownership. SORA implemented a 1:100 XOR redenomination coordinated through on-chain governance to simplify pricing, rebalance treasury reserves, and prepare for the token bonding curve monetary system.

terms.title: Sumeragi Consensus
terms.summary: The formal HotStuff-style guarantees—safety, liveness, and QC intersection—embedded in the SUMERAGI pipeline.
terms.definition: The formal HotStuff-style guarantees—safety, liveness, and QC intersection—embedded in the SUMERAGI pipeline.
terms.tagline: Provides mathematical proof that committed blocks cannot be reverted, even under network partitions.

terms.title: SUMERAGI Pipeline

terms.definition: The multi-stage HotStuff-like process in Iroha 3 that sequences proposals, votes, and commits per lane.

terms.title: Supply Management
terms.summary: Supply management encompasses all mechanisms controlling token issuance, burning, and circulation. SORA uses the Token Bonding Curve, fee burns, and strategic reserves to maintain healthy token economics.
terms.definition: Supply management encompasses all mechanisms controlling token issuance, burning, and circulation. SORA uses the Token Bonding Curve, fee burns, and strategic reserves to maintain healthy token economics.

terms.title: Supply Reduction
terms.summary: Supply reduction refers to mechanisms that decrease the circulating supply of tokens over time, including burns, lockups, and deflationary tokenomics. SORA implements supply reduction through transaction fee burns and buyback programs.
terms.definition: Supply reduction refers to mechanisms that decrease the circulating supply of tokens over time, including burns, lockups, and deflationary tokenomics. SORA implements supply reduction through transaction fee burns and buyback programs.

terms.title: Supranational Platform
terms.summary: A blockchain platform that operates above the level of individual nation states, enabling global coordination and collaboration without being subject to any single country's jur…
terms.definition: A blockchain platform that operates above the level of individual nation states, enabling global coordination and collaboration without being subject to any single country's jurisdiction. SORA v3 serves as a supranational platform that de-correlates CBDCs and government-issued digital assets from political and economic instability, providing a stable foundation for global transactions. This design enables nations, institutions, and individuals to create assets and conduct transactions on a borderless, decentralized infrastructure.

terms.title: Syscalls
terms.summary: Limited, 8-bit-indexed entry points exposed by the IVM for operations like hashing or storage, each with deterministic gas cost.
terms.definition: Limited, 8-bit-indexed entry points exposed by the IVM for operations like hashing or storage, each with deterministic gas cost.
terms.tagline: Provides a secure, auditable interface between smart contracts and the underlying runtime.

terms.title: Taikai
terms.summary: The streaming and data pipeline platform governed on-ledger, supporting Norito streaming, telemetry, and slashing for misbehavior.
terms.definition: The streaming and data pipeline platform governed on-ledger, supporting Norito streaming, telemetry, and slashing for misbehavior.
terms.tagline: Enables misbehavior.

terms.title: TBCD
terms.summary: Token Bonding Curve Dollar (TBCD) is an algorithmic, non-synthetic stablecoin whose value is maintained by the SORA token bonding curve at approximately $1 USD. TBCD is converti…
terms.definition: Token Bonding Curve Dollar (TBCD) is an algorithmic, non-synthetic stablecoin whose value is maintained by the SORA token bonding curve at approximately $1 USD. TBCD is convertible to XOR as a reserve asset of the token bonding curve and helps build up reserves while also being used to fund the creation of new goods and services via on-chain governance. In SORA v3 tokenomics, 0.5% of all network transaction fees are allocated for buyback and burning of TBCD. TBCD can only be created and allocated by on-chain governance, meaning XOR token holders decide the supply.
terms.tagline: Offers algorithmic stability through the token bonding curve mechanism.

terms.title: Telegram
terms.summary: Telegram is the primary chat channel where the SORA community coordinates releases, support, validator updates, and governance calls.
terms.definition: Telegram is the primary chat channel where the SORA community coordinates releases, support, validator updates, and governance calls.

terms.title: Telemetry
terms.summary: The observability feeds - lane latency, DA failures, breaker status - that operators monitor to keep Nexus healthy.
terms.definition: The observability feeds - lane latency, DA failures, breaker status - that operators monitor to keep Nexus healthy.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Three-Hop QUIC Circuits
terms.summary: SoraNet's onion-style routing pattern using QUIC, providing low-latency privacy with fixed hop counts.
terms.definition: SoraNet's onion-style routing pattern using QUIC, providing low-latency privacy with fixed hop counts.
terms.tagline: Hides user IP addresses from destination servers while maintaining fast connections.

terms.title: Token Bonding Curve
terms.summary: A smart contract that manages the supply of XOR in a rational way without human involvement. The TBC automatically adjusts XOR supply based on economic conditions to maintain pr…
terms.definition: A smart contract that manages the supply of XOR in a rational way without human involvement. The TBC automatically adjusts XOR supply based on economic conditions to maintain price stability, expanding supply during growth and contracting during decline.
terms.tagline: Creates predictable pricing and built-in liquidity for XOR without requiring external market makers.

terms.title: Token Burning
terms.summary: The permanent removal of tokens from circulation by sending them to an unrecoverable address. In SORA, token burning is used as a deflationary mechanism - VAL tokens are burned …
terms.definition: The permanent removal of tokens from circulation by sending them to an unrecoverable address. In SORA, token burning is used as a deflationary mechanism - VAL tokens are burned on every network transaction, and PSWAP tokens are burned on every Polkaswap transaction to reduce supply over time.

terms.title: Tokenization
terms.summary: The conversion of rights to an asset into a digital token on a blockchain. Tokenization underpins SORA's strategy of turning real-world economic activity into programmable, composable assets.
terms.definition: Tokenization abstracts ownership or utility into blockchain-based tokens that can be traded, fractionally owned, or used as collateral. It is a foundational capability for SORA's knowledge base, enabling CBDCs, RWAs, and incentive programs to interoperate within the Polkaswap ecosystem.

terms.title: Tokenized Assets
terms.summary: A use case where real-world assets are issued in data spaces with deterministic policy, proofs, and ISO-aligned connectors.
terms.definition: A use case where real-world assets are issued in data spaces with deterministic policy, proofs, and ISO-aligned connectors.
terms.tagline: Essential component of the SORA Nexus architecture.

terms.title: Tokenomics
terms.summary: Tokenomics explores supply design, burn models, and incentive loops that guide SORA’s economic roadmap.
terms.definition: Tokenomics explores supply design, burn models, and incentive loops that guide SORA’s economic roadmap.

terms.title: Token Repackaging
terms.summary: An initiative in the SORA roadmap to migrate legacy assets into a simplified portfolio of utility, reward, and stable tokens that align with the SORA v3 economic model.
terms.definition: Token repackaging consolidates historical SORA and Polkaswap assets into a streamlined set of instruments—XOR for settlement, VAL for validator rewards, PSWAP for liquidity incentives, and new stable instruments such as TBCD. The program retires illiquid or redundant tokens, migrates balances, and funds ecosystem development through governance-approved conversions.

terms.title: TON
terms.summary: TON (The Open Network) is a Telegram-backed blockchain known for high throughput and mobile-native UX that now powers TONSwap's SORA-linked DeFi.
terms.definition: TON (The Open Network) is a Telegram-backed blockchain known for high throughput and mobile-native UX that now powers TONSwap's SORA-linked DeFi.

terms.title: Tonswap
terms.summary: A next-generation decentralized exchange (DEX) and launchpad built on The Open Network (TON) blockchain. TONSWAP combines cutting-edge concentrated liquidity technology with a u…
terms.definition: A next-generation decentralized exchange (DEX) and launchpad built on The Open Network (TON) blockchain. TONSWAP combines cutting-edge concentrated liquidity technology with a user-friendly design, offering ultra-fast trades, near-zero fees, and seamless Telegram integration. It serves as a TON-native gateway for mobile-first DeFi access. TONSWAP creates sustained on-chain demand for XOR tokens by automatically allocating 10% of all trading fees to buy back and burn XOR, connecting TON ecosystem activity to the SORA economy.
terms.tagline: Expands SORA DeFi reach to Telegram users through TON integration.

terms.title: Torii
terms.summary: The Norito-native gateway streaming events, receipts, and telemetry to clients via REST, SSE, or gRPC.
terms.definition: The Norito-native gateway streaming events, receipts, and telemetry to clients via REST, SSE, or gRPC.
terms.tagline: Provides real-time updates to applications without polling.

terms.title: Trading
terms.summary: Trading on SORA encompasses swapping tokens on Polkaswap, providing liquidity to pools, and participating in price discovery through the DEX. The network supports multiple liquidity sources and algorithmic pricing for efficient markets.
terms.definition: Trading on SORA encompasses swapping tokens on Polkaswap, providing liquidity to pools, and participating in price discovery through the DEX. The network supports multiple liquidity sources and algorithmic pricing for efficient markets.

terms.title: Trading Fees
terms.summary: Charges applied to trading transactions on decentralized exchanges. In SORA, trading fees on Polkaswap are used for various purposes including PSWAP buyback-and-burn (0.3%), val…
terms.definition: Charges applied to trading transactions on decentralized exchanges. In SORA, trading fees on Polkaswap are used for various purposes including PSWAP buyback-and-burn (0.3%), validator rewards, and network maintenance.

terms.title: Trading Strategy
terms.summary: A framework for entering and exiting markets to achieve risk-adjusted returns. Polkaswap traders use strategies to balance liquidity mining, arbitrage, and long-term positioning.
terms.definition: Trading strategies outline rules for portfolio allocation, order placement, and risk management. In SORA, strategies can combine Polkaswap swaps, liquidity provision, and staking to capture yield while supporting ecosystem liquidity.

terms.title: Transaction Execution Units (TEU)
terms.summary: The resource metric measuring instruction cost, bandwidth, and storage to drive scheduling and fee calculation.
terms.definition: The resource metric measuring instruction cost, bandwidth, and storage to drive scheduling and fee calculation.
terms.tagline: Lets users predict transaction costs before submitting, preventing surprise fees.

terms.title: Transaction Lifecycle
terms.summary: The six-stage flow - submission, admission, execution, aggregation, consensus, exposure - that every Nexus transaction follows.
terms.definition: The six-stage flow - submission, admission, execution, aggregation, consensus, exposure - that every Nexus transaction follows.
terms.tagline: Every Nexus transaction follows.

terms.title: Triggers
terms.summary: On-ledger automation objects with condition, action, and budget fields that execute schedules or reactions without off-chain cron jobs.
terms.definition: On-ledger automation objects with condition, action, and budget fields that execute schedules or reactions without off-chain cron jobs.
terms.tagline: Enables smart contracts to self-execute based on time or events, removing reliance on external keepers.

terms.title: Ts
terms.summary: The platform token for TONSWAP, a decentralized exchange and launchpad on The Open Network (TON).
terms.definition: TS grants governance rights and distributes incentives on TONSWAP, the TON-based DEX that integrates with SORA liquidity programs. Holders can participate in fee distribution and vote on protocol upgrades that affect listings and incentive schedules.

terms.title: Two-Dimensional Erasure Coding
terms.summary: The matrix-style Reed - Solomon scheme (rows and columns) SoraFS uses to ensure any subset of shards can rebuild the original data.
terms.definition: The matrix-style Reed - Solomon scheme (rows and columns) SoraFS uses to ensure any subset of shards can rebuild the original data.
terms.tagline: Essential component of the SORA Nexus architecture.

terms.title: VAL
terms.summary: A validator reward token for the SORA network used to reward validators and stake nominators. VAL has deflationary tokenomics with tokens burned on every transaction, and elasti…
terms.definition: A validator reward token for the SORA network used to reward validators and stake nominators. VAL has deflationary tokenomics with tokens burned on every transaction, and elastic rewards distributed as a percentage of daily burned tokens.
terms.tagline: Incentivizes network security through deflationary rewards to validators and nominators.

terms.title: Validator
terms.summary: A network participant that validates transactions and maintains the blockchain. Validators in SORA secure the network and earn rewards for their services.
terms.definition: A network participant that validates transactions and maintains the blockchain. Validators in SORA secure the network and earn rewards for their services.

terms.title: Validators
terms.summary: Validators are network operators who stake tokens to produce blocks, validate transactions, and maintain consensus. SORA validators earn VAL rewards for securing the network and processing state transitions.
terms.definition: Validators are network operators who stake tokens to produce blocks, validate transactions, and maintain consensus. SORA validators earn VAL rewards for securing the network and processing state transitions.

terms.title: Vault
terms.summary: A vault is a smart contract that securely holds collateral for minting synthetic assets or stablecoins. On SORA, Kensetsu vaults allow users to deposit XOR, VAL, or other assets to borrow KUSD.
terms.definition: A vault is a smart contract that securely holds collateral for minting synthetic assets or stablecoins. On SORA, Kensetsu vaults allow users to deposit XOR, VAL, or other assets to borrow KUSD.

terms.title: Vaults
terms.summary: Smart-contract containers that manage pooled assets. Vaults underpin planned Kensetsu money markets and Polkaswap liquidity programs.
terms.definition: Vaults automate strategies such as lending, liquidity provision, or reward distribution. In SORA, vaults will back Kensetsu stablecoins, manage collateral, and automate treasury deployments.

terms.title: Volatility
terms.summary: A measure of how widely an asset's price fluctuates over a period of time.
terms.definition: Volatility quantifies price dispersion using metrics such as standard deviation or implied volatility from derivatives markets. Higher volatility signals greater uncertainty and risk, influencing position sizing and hedging decisions for SORA participants.

terms.title: Voting
terms.summary: Voting is the act of citizens or stakeholders signaling support for SORA governance proposals through on-chain referenda or delegated councils.
terms.definition: Voting is the act of citizens or stakeholders signaling support for SORA governance proposals through on-chain referenda or delegated councils.

terms.title: VRF Aggregate
terms.summary: The combined verifiable random function output from committees, feeding epoch beacons and lane-specific randomness.
terms.definition: The combined verifiable random function output from committees, feeding epoch beacons and lane-specific randomness.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: VRF Sortition
terms.summary: A method for drawing validator committees where candidates prove via VRF that their random output meets a threshold.
terms.definition: A method for drawing validator committees where candidates prove via VRF that their random output meets a threshold.
terms.tagline: Prevents validator collusion by making committee selection unpredictable until the moment of reveal.

terms.title: Wallet
terms.summary: A wallet is the software that stores keys, signs transactions, and connects users to SORA DeFi apps such as Polkaswap, Fearless Wallet, or TONSwap.
terms.definition: A wallet is the software that stores keys, signs transactions, and connects users to SORA DeFi apps such as Polkaswap, Fearless Wallet, or TONSwap.

terms.title: WASM (WebAssembly)
terms.summary: A portable binary instruction format that enables high-performance smart contracts and runtime modules.
terms.definition: WebAssembly lets blockchain runtimes execute code securely and efficiently across platforms. Hyperledger Iroha 3 uses WASM for domain-specific smart instructions, and many SORA ecosystem tools compile to WASM for browser compatibility.

terms.title: Web3
terms.summary: The next iteration of the internet where decentralized protocols give users ownership over identity, assets, and coordination.
terms.definition: Web3 combines blockchain, decentralized storage, and smart contracts to deliver user-owned networks. SORA positions itself as a Web3 supranational economy that blends DeFi, governance, and real-world integrations.

terms.title: World State View (WSV)
terms.summary: The canonical state database holding current balances, metadata, and trigger definitions across all data spaces.
terms.definition: The canonical state database holding current balances, metadata, and trigger definitions across all data spaces.
terms.tagline: Gives every validator a consistent snapshot of network state, enabling instant balance queries.

terms.title: Xcm
terms.summary: Cross-Consensus Messaging - a messaging format that allows different consensus systems to communicate with each other. XCM enables interoperability between parachains in the Pol…
terms.definition: Cross-Consensus Messaging - a messaging format that allows different consensus systems to communicate with each other. XCM enables interoperability between parachains in the Polkadot ecosystem, allowing SORA to communicate with other parachains.

terms.title: Xcmp
terms.summary: Polkadot's Cross-Chain Message Passing protocol for parachain-to-parachain communication.
terms.definition: XCMP allows parachains to exchange messages directly while relying on the relay chain for ordering and security. It underpins trust-minimized asset transfers and remote calls, enabling SORA-aligned parachains to interoperate with the wider Polkadot ecosystem.

terms.title: XOR
terms.summary: The network utility token used for transaction fees (gas) where 50% of fees are burned and 50% go to validators. XOR has elastic supply managed by a token bonding curve and can …
terms.definition: The network utility token used for transaction fees (gas) where 50% of fees are burned and 50% go to validators. XOR has elastic supply managed by a token bonding curve and can be used for staking, liquidity provision, and future SORA Parliament membership.
terms.tagline: Powers every transaction on SORA and gives holders governance rights in the network.

terms.title: XOR Bonds
terms.summary: Stake deposits in XOR that governance proposals or data-space onboardings must lock to align incentives.
terms.definition: Stake deposits in XOR that governance proposals or data-space onboardings must lock to align incentives.
terms.tagline: Empowers the community to shape the network's evolution.

terms.title: XOR Fee Equilibrium
terms.summary: The economic model that balances lane demand, TEU costs, and fee floors so XOR rewards stay predictable.
terms.definition: The economic model that balances lane demand, TEU costs, and fee floors so XOR rewards stay predictable.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: XOR Utility
terms.summary: The multi-role nature of XOR as fee token, settlement asset, collateral, and governance bond across data spaces.
terms.definition: The multi-role nature of XOR as fee token, settlement asset, collateral, and governance bond across data spaces.
terms.tagline: Creates natural demand for XOR through its essential role in every network operation.

terms.title: XYK Pools

terms.definition: Constant Product Market Maker (CPMM) liquidity pools where the product of two token reserves remains constant (x * y = k). These are the primary liquidity pools on Polkaswap where users can provide liquidity and earn PSWAP rewards through yield farming.

terms.title: Yield Farming
terms.summary: A DeFi strategy where users provide liquidity to protocols and earn rewards. In Polkaswap, users can farm PSWAP tokens by providing liquidity to XYK pools, with rewards distribu…
terms.definition: A DeFi strategy where users provide liquidity to protocols and earn rewards. In Polkaswap, users can farm PSWAP tokens by providing liquidity to XYK pools, with rewards distributed through the platform's liquidity aggregation system. Polkaswap's unique infrastructure reduces impermanent loss risks while providing competitive yields through multi-source liquidity aggregation.

terms.title: ZK-Backed Access Tickets

terms.definition: Proof-carrying credentials in SoraNet that grant network access while obscuring user identity or route.
terms.tagline: Grant network access while obscuring user identity or route.

terms.definition: Zero-knowledge proofs that bind erasure-coded shards to block commitments, proving availability without revealing private data.
terms.tagline: Guarantees that transaction data remains accessible and verifiable.
